factorSources.note: The Infatuation calls the sausage-pepper-provolone pie the standout, with a crisp, chewy crust; Seattle Times restaurant critic Providence Cicero, quoted on MyNorthwest's Let's Eat segment, praised the 'fabulous' salads and said the pie toppings are always inventive.

The Stranger profiled the worker-owned Madison Park shop as a tight, open-kitchen neighborhood joint; Seattle Weekly praised its Neapolitan-meets-NYC crust and kid-friendly menu despite the cramped room and slow service from a small staff.

The Infatuation (8.7) calls the vodka-sauce 'Mr. Pink' pie the standout, with a thick, heavily charred crust; The Stranger's head-to-head slice comparison ranked it first among nine Seattle pizzerias for its square, New Jersey-style slice.

The Infatuation rates it 7.6, calling it a 'middle-tier Neapolitan spot' on Capitol Hill that isn't the neighborhood's top pizza pick but holds its own, recommending the spicy salami pie and a buffalo mozzarella upgrade on the margherita.

The Infatuation rates it 7.3 and calls the Columbia City location one of the best sit-down meals in the neighborhood, singling out the margherita as the standout pie and noting the crust holds up better to wet toppings with extra oven time.
